identity.title: The Deuterium Fraction in Massive Starless Cores and Dynamical Implications

paper_type_evidence.quote: In this paper we use the *ALMA* data from T13 (see their paper for more details of these observations).

evidence.quote: core physical radius at a distance of 5 kpc
core physical radius at a distance of 5 kpc

question.value: What are the deuterium fractions of N2H+ in two massive starless cores, and what collapse rate relative to free-fall do they imply via chemodynamical modeling?

evidence.quote: We then present chemodynamical modeling of the two cores, exploring especially the implications for the collapse rate relative to free-fall, $\alpha_{\rm ff}$.
This paper makes use of the following *ALMA* data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00236.S.
The angular resolution of *ALMA* observation is 2$''$, and the maximum recoverable scale is 9$''$.
The two cores were first detected by $\rm N_2D^+$(3-2) emission in *ALMA* Cycle 0 observations (T13).
We observed the cores in $\rm N_2H^+$(1-0) at 93 GHz with the *CARMA* 15-element array
We observed ortho-H$_2$D$^+$ J$_{k^+,k^-}$ = 1$_{1,0}$ $\rightarrow$ 1$_{1,1}$ and $\rm N_2H^+$(4-3) lines
We observed $\rm N_2D^+$(1-0) at 77 GHz, with a beam size of $\sim$22$''$.
The *IRAM 30m* data of $\rm N_2D^+$(2-1) and $\rm N_2H^+$(3-2) presented in this paper are taken from (cite: 2011A&A...529L...7F).
SMA observations were made as part of the “SMA survey of high-mass starless cores” in the most compact configuration (sub-compact)

what.value: Core properties (radii, LSR velocities, dispersions, mass surface density, densities, masses) from ALMA N2D+(3-2) and 1.3 mm continuum

evidence.quote: Core properties defined by *ALMA* observations of $\rm N_2D^+$(3-2) by T13
The *IRAM 30m* data of $\rm N_2D^+$(2-1) and $\rm N_2H^+$(3-2) presented in this paper are taken from (cite: 2011A&A...529L...7F).

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Astrochemical collapse models from K15 compared with observed abundances

evidence.quote: We run astrochemical models developed by (cite: 2015ApJ...804...98K) to compare with the above observational results.

flux_scale_uncertainty.value: ALMA ≲20%; CARMA ~15%; JCMT ≲20%; NRO ~10%; IRAM ~20%; SMA ~15%

evidence.quote: we note also that the calibration uncertainties of these data are estimated to be $\lesssim 20\%$
Overall flux calibration uncertainties are estimate to be $\sim 15\%$.

primary_beam_correction.value: efficiency correction, roughly factor of 2.0 for C1-S, not done in T13

evidence.quote: so we applied a primary beam efficiency correction (roughly a factor of 2.0, depending on distance from phase center) to the observed fluxes
The synthesized beam is 5.5$''$ $\times$ 4.7$''$ with P.A. = 4$^\circ$.
The final 1$\sigma$ rms at the map center for C1 is 0.050 Jy beam$^{-1}$ (combined CDE-configuration).
In this paper we use the *ALMA* data from T13 (see their paper for more details of these observations).
Other parameters of the modeling are the same as those listed in Tables 1 and 2 of K15.
We follow (cite: 2003A&A...403L..37C) to calculate the column density.
Further details on the observing and imaging will be reported in a separate publication on the survey (Pillai et al. in prep.).
